In mathematics, the '''length of an element''' ''w'' in a [[Weyl group]] ''W'', denoted by ''l''(''w''), is the smallest number ''k'' so that ''w'' is a product of ''k'' reflections by simple roots. (So, the notion depends on the choice of a [[positive Weyl chamber]].) In particular, a simple reflection has length one. The function ''l'' is then an integer-valued function of ''W''; it is a [[length function]] of&nbsp;''W''. It follows immediately from the definition that ''l''(''w''<sup>−1</sup>) = ''l''(''w'') and that ''l''(''ww''<nowiki>'</nowiki><sup>−1</sup>) ≤ ''l''(''w'') + ''l''(''w' '').

{{See also|Longest element of a Coxeter group}}
